findings.title: Accidental submodule/gitlink added
findings.body: The PR adds a gitlink/submodule (`Subproject commit ...`) at repository root. This is unrelated to the feature and can break checkouts/builds or accidentally vendor another repository. It should be removed.

findings.title: Eligibility cache has no effective invalidation
findings.body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` caches allowlist eligibility for 60 seconds, but nothing invalidates these keys when `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` changes. The unused `invalidate_upsampling_cache` helper also only deletes one exact project-set key. If the allowlist changes, API responses can return upsampled or non-upsampled counts incorrectly for up to a minute.

findings.title: Cache key uses Python hash() of project IDs
findings.body: The cache key embeds `hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))`. Python hash values are not a stable, collision-resistant way to build cache keys across processes/versions, and different project sets could collide. Use a deterministic key such as sorted project IDs joined together.

findings.title: Error-only detection is a naive substring match
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` treats any occurrence of `event.type:error` in the raw query as an error-only query. This matches negated filters like `!event.type:error`, OR clauses that also include transactions, and text/tag values. For discover queries this can replace `count()` with `upsampled_count()` when non-error events are included, producing wrong counts.

findings.title: upsampled_count is exposed as a public aggregate
findings.body: The new `upsampled_count` SnQL function is not marked `private=True`, unlike neighboring internal functions. API callers may be able to request it directly, bypassing the allowlist/eligibility logic that only rewrites `count()`, and get incorrect results on projects or datasets where sample weights should not be used.

findings.title: upsampled_count does not handle missing sample_weight
findings.body: `upsampled_count` is implemented as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`. If any queried event has NULL/missing `sample_weight` (for example historical events before upsampling was enabled, malformed events, or non-error rows accidentally included in discover), the aggregation can ignore those rows or return NULL/zero, silently changing counts. A fallback or explicit row filtering is needed.

findings.title: Upsampling can be enabled for errors dataset without function registration
findings.body: `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns true for the errors dataset, but the PR only registers `upsampled_count` in the discover dataset converter. If the errors dataset does not inherit that converter, allowlisted requests using `dataset=errors` will generate queries referencing an unknown function and fail.

findings.title: Upsampling decision uses request dataset instead of executed dataset
findings.body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset` but determines upsampling using the outer `dataset` captured from the request. When the factory substitutes a split dataset (for example dashboard widget split queries), the eligibility check can be based on the wrong dataset, causing the transform to be applied or skipped incorrectly.

findings.title: Top-events path only transforms timeseries columns
findings.body: For `topEvents > 0`, the PR transforms `timeseries_columns`/`y_axes` but leaves `selected_columns`, `equations`, and `orderby` untransformed. If those fields contain or depend on `count()`, top-event selection/ordering may use raw counts while returned timeseries use upsampled counts, making rankings and values inconsistent.

findings.title: Tests miss high-risk upsampling paths
findings.body: The endpoint tests cover only simple discover queries with explicit `event.type:error`. They do not cover `dataset=errors`, top events, dashboard split queries, negated/ambiguous event.type conditions, direct use of `upsampled_count()`, or cache expiry/invalidation. These are the paths most likely to expose incorrect counts or query failures.
